ION Clean Energy 39 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 11 Techno-Economic Analysis ION was tasked with developing a Techno-Economic Assessment based on the Bituminous Baseline Study (BBS) cases developed by DOE/NETL. S&L was engaged by ION to prepare the TEA using performance and process design information specific to the ICE-31® solvent technology. This TEA was originally prepared in 2020 and has been revised based on operational data of the pilot facility, including key learnings identified during the DE-FE0031950 project. The purpose of the TEA is to evaluate the economic feasibility of implementing the ION carbon capture system at a greenfield power plant equipped with a natural gas combustion turbine, heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), and steam turbine. Capital costs, operating and maintenance (O&M) costs, and the cost of electricity (COE) were prepared by the Department of Energy (DOE) and National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL) and published in the BBS in 2019 revision (Rev 4). The objective of the BBS case studies is to determine the comparative costs of electricity at various types of green-field power facilities. Case 31A is reflective of an F-class NGCC facility without a carbon capture system; Case 31B is reflective of an F-class NGCC facility utilizing carbon capture. The carbon capture system chosen for the BBS Case 31B is the Shell Cansolv system, which is considered a state-of-the-art full-scale application. The ION TEA compares the incremental increase in COE and cost of capture (in $/tCO ) for the ION system based on the 2 comparative costs estimated by the DOE between BBS Case 31A to BBS Case 31B. The footprint of the capture plant, including its balance of plant equipment, is approximately equivalent to the base NGCC power plant. This economic evaluation was conducted according to the design basis laid out in the BBS Case 31B to the best extent possible. However, several technical and operational parameters within this TEA for ION’s carbon capture system are based on the results of the pilot system using ION’s proprietary advanced solvent, ICE-31®. Furthermore, costs and design elements from a recent front-end engineering and design (FEED) study were adjusted for the NGCC application. The capital costs estimate is broken into bare erected costs, total plant cost, and total overnight cost. O&M costs are broken into variable and fixed O&M. Ultimately the annualized capital costs are combined with the O&M costs to determine the lifecycle cost of the facility. All costs are reported in December 2018 dollars.
